chunks: 1666 - Sama'ah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The specified right is not from zakat. It is something that you bring out from your wealth, if you wish, every Friday, and if you wish, every month. And for every possessor of bounty there is his due measure of bounty. And the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“And if you conceal it and give it to the poor, then it is better for you.”

So it is not from zakat. And al-māʿūn is not from zakat; it is the kindness that you do, the loan that you lend, the household goods that you loan out, and maintaining ties with your relatives—it is not from zakat. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“And those in whose wealth there is a known right.”

So the specified right is other than zakat, and it is something a man makes obligatory upon himself, that it be from his wealth and himself, and it is incumbent upon him to assign it according to the measure of his ability and his means.”

key_terms.اَلزَّكَاةِ: The obligatory alms-tax, which the hadith distinguishes from other forms of giving.
key_terms.اَلْحَقُّ الْمَعْلُومُ: A specified and recognized right in one’s wealth, distinct from zakat.
key_terms.اَلْقَرْضُ: A loan given to another person.
key_terms.اَلْمَاعُونُ: Neighborly and social assistance, such as lending useful items and helping others.
key_terms.اَلْمَعْرُوفُ: An act of recognized kindness or goodness done for others.
key_terms.سَعَتِهِ: A person’s means or breadth of resources.
key_terms.صِلَةُ قَرَابَتِكَ: Maintaining ties and support for one’s relatives.

ai.seo_question: What is al-ḥaqq al-maʿlūm, and how is it different from zakat in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that al-ḥaqq al-maʿlūm is a charitable due distinct from zakat, one that a person voluntarily commits upon himself according to his capacity. It also explains al-māʿūn as everyday acts of assistance such as lending, helping, and maintaining kinship ties, and connects both meanings to Qur'anic verses about giving and recognized rights in wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1666 - Sama'ah narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"The specified right (al-haqq al-ma‘loom) is not part of Zakat. It is something you give from your wealth, if you wish, every Friday, or if you wish, every month. For every person of means, there is an obligation according to their capacity.
Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: 'If you conceal it and give it to the poor, it is better for you' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:271).

This is not part of Zakat.
As for al-ma‘oon (neighborly assistance), it is also not part of Zakat. It is the kindness you show, the loan you offer, the household items you lend, and the support you give to your relatives—it is not part of Zakat.
Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: 'And those who in their wealth acknowledge a recognized right' (Surah Al-Ma’arij 70:24).
This recognized right is separate from Zakat. It is something a person imposes upon himself, to be taken from his wealth and provided according to his capacity and resources."
